editorial:
Imagine being a lonely kid who gets picked on every single day at school. That is exactly where you find Owen, a shy boy who feels like he has no one in the world. Everything changes when a mysterious girl named Abby moves in next door. She seems like a normal kid at first, but she only comes out at night and has a strange adult guardian who does her dirty work. You will feel the cold, snowy mood of the neighborhood as these two form a bond over their shared loneliness. It is not your typical jump-scare horror movie; instead, it is a slow-burn story about friendship and the scary things people do to survive.

The acting is great, especially from the kids who make the relationship feel real and sad. You will love how the tension builds up toward the end, though some might find the middle a bit slow. If you enjoy stories that mix sadness with a bit of blood, you should definitely check this out. It looks amazing in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you have the option, but renting it on Apple TV is also a quick way to see it. For movie buffs, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: At the end, Abby protects Owen by killing his bullies in a violent way. Owen knows she is a monster, but he loves her anyway. They decide to leave their town together to start a new life. As they ride a train away, Owen lets Abby bite him so she can feed. They leave behind a trail of bodies, showing that their love is dark and dangerous, but they are finally together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark fairy tales and emotional horror stories.
